:::{#def-line-search}
#### Line search and exact line search

In gradient descent (@def-gradient-descent),
a **line search** is a rule that chooses the step length $s^{(t)}$
by examining the values of $f$ along the line
$\cb{\vx^{(t)} - s\,\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)}) : s > 0}$.
**Exact line search** is the line search that chooses $s^{(t)}$
to minimize $f(\vx^{(t)} - s\,\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)}))$ over $s > 0$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-line-search}
#### Exact line search on a parabola

For $f(x) = x^2$ and $x^{(t)} = 2$, the derivative is $f'(2) = 4$,
so the line is $\cb{2 - 4s : s > 0}$ and the values along it are

$$
\ba
\linefn(s)
&= f(2 - 4s)
&& \text{(the value at step length } s \text{)}
\\&= (2 - 4s)^2
&& (f(x) = x^2)
\ea
$$

$\linefn(s) \ge 0$ for every $s$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\linefn(0.5) &= (2 - 2)^2 \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so exact line search chooses $s^{(t)} = 0.5$,
which lands on the minimizer $x^{(t+1)} = 0$ in one step.

:::
